title: VPC deploy environment verifier: Terraform-friendly pre-deploy sanity checks
creator: Ethan Morales
description: Build an automated 'environment verifier' that runs as part of Terraform/CI pre-deploy for Private (VPC) installs. The verifier will surface quota, IAM, DNS, network, and GPU capacity problems before customer installs proceed, provide actionable remediation steps, and emit structured results that the Console and onboarding scripts can consume.
tasks: Design verifier API and output schema (JSON) for terraform-external-data and CI
Implement cloud-specific checks: AWS (quotas, IAM roles, VPC/cidr collisions, Route53 private hosted zones), GCP (quotas, IAM, private DNS), Azure (quotas, RBAC, private dns zones)
GPU inventory check: per-AZ available instance types, vendor driver/AMI compatibility hints, total GPU count vs requested pool size
Create Terraform module wrapper that calls verifier as external data source and fails apply with readable error links
Add smoke-run step to Private deployment docs and onboarding scripts that parses verifier output and prints remediation steps
Integrate verifier results to Console onboarding checklist and add metric/event for failures
acceptance_criteria: Verifier returns deterministic JSON exit code and a human-readable summary for any check failure
Terraform wrapper consumes verifier and aborts plan/apply when critical failures are detected
Checks cover at minimum: service quotas, required IAM roles/policies, ability to create private DNS records, reachable VPC endpoints, and GPU capacity per-AZ
Automated test harness with mocked cloud APIs validates failure modes and recovery guidance
Documentation and runbook added to Private deploy docs with example outputs and remediation steps
design_decisions: Output format: compact JSON with fields (status, severity, check_id, message, remediation_links)
Expose verifier via two interfaces: cli binary (go) for local runs and terraform-external-data provider for CI
Priority mapping: critical failures (quota exhausted, missing IAM create perms, no GPUs in any AZ) fail terraform; warnings (soft quota, dns eventual consistency) surfaced but do not block by default
GPU check will prefer exact instance family matching requested runtime profile and fall back to closest supported family with explicit warning
Do not attempt to alter customer account state (no automated quota increase). Provide exact console links and command snippets for remediation
